ReflectMe — feedback and reflection experience

The idea

The gap between who you think you are and who others experience.

ReflectMe came from a simple question: what if you could understand how the people around you actually experience you, without having to guess?

The product lets people collect honest reflections from people who know them. Feedback can be anonymous or named, while the recipient decides what becomes public and what stays private.

Product thinking

Designing for honesty without making it uncomfortable.

01

Privacy by default

The person receiving feedback controls what is public and what remains private. There are no surprise public reveals.

02

Quiet by design

The experience is intentionally reflective rather than noisy, gamified, or built around conventional social-media behaviour.

03

Useful reflection

Feedback is structured into an experience that helps users spot patterns rather than simply accumulate comments.

What I built

From a simple feedback form to a product.

Public profiles

A personal profile gives people a simple place to understand the person, see shared reflections, and request feedback.

Structured feedback

Feedback is collected through structured prompts rather than an open-ended comment box, making responses easier to interpret.

Privacy controls

Anonymous and named feedback are supported, with the recipient controlling the visibility of individual reflections.

Reflection dashboard

Feedback is brought together into an overview that makes recurring themes and patterns easier to see.

Engineering

Building trust into the system.

For a product dealing with personal feedback, the engineering decisions are closely tied to the experience. Privacy, access control, and clarity are product features, not implementation details.

React application

A component-based React frontend with reusable UI patterns and Tailwind/CSS variables forming the visual system.

Supabase backend

Supabase provides the application backend and persistence layer, with the product deployed through Vercel.

AI-assisted insights

Feedback patterns can be summarized into a short AI-generated overview, with generated text and its timestamp cached so revisiting a profile does not repeatedly call the model.

Discoverability

The product includes deliberate page metadata, sitemap support, and search-console setup rather than treating SEO as an afterthought.

Architecture

A small product with a real system behind it.

Reflection

The hardest part wasn't collecting feedback.

The harder product problem was creating an environment where people would actually be comfortable giving honest feedback.

That shaped everything from the quiet visual language to anonymity, visibility controls, and the decision to keep the product reflective rather than turning it into another public social network.
